body:
Chief: THE OWNER'S CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED IN FULL AND MY DISPOSITION WAS WRONG ON REQUIREMENT 1. I called dynamic surface detail "an unexposed parameter, not a design gap" and "nearly free". It is neither.

WHAT I CHECKED AND WHAT I INFERRED, because the difference is the whole error. I verified that SurfaceDetail.Hidden is hardcoded in three production places and that the axis has never varied in any artifact. That is true. I then INFERRED that the axis was implemented and merely unexposed. I never checked whether VARYING it changes anything. Those are different claims and I only tested the first.

THE OWNER RAN THE PROBE I SHOULD HAVE. Compile the WOG Scene view three times at Hidden, Sentences and Tokens: mark counts 83, 83, 83; hidden.marks == sentences.marks; hidden.marks == tokens.marks; navigation equal across all three; selectionPlacements equal across all three. AND THREE DISTINCT CONFIGURATION CHECKSUMS. AtlasCompiler reads spec.zoom.narrative at atlas.scala:366, and the only production uses of spec.zoom.surface are the configuration checksum at :770 and the textual twin at :793. Nothing branches on the enum in mark compilation.

SO SurfaceDetail IS A GHOST AXIS - RECEIPTED BUT SEMANTICALLY INERT. That is not "unexposed", it is "does not exist below the receipt".

AND THE CHECKSUM RESULT IS A SEPARATE DEFECT WORTH NAMING ON ITS OWN, because it is tonight's disease running in reverse. Every other finding has been DISTINCT THINGS COLLAPSED INTO ONE NUMBER - unranked and observed, ineligible and missing, two coverage fields that were one measurement. This is ONE THING MINTED AS THREE IDENTITIES. Three configuration checksums for byte-identical representations means the receipt DISTINGUISHES WHAT IS NOT DIFFERENT, and a consumer comparing two runs by checksum would conclude the representation changed when it did not. Same class, opposite sign, and I would not have looked for it.

THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE THE OWNER DREW IS THE RIGHT ONE AND I AM ADOPTING IT: simply adding a StoryAtlas selector would be actively harmful - it would mint three receipts and three titles for one picture and LOOK like the feature had shipped. Do not begin with the control.

REVISED DISPOSITION ON REQUIREMENT 1: it is NOT nearly free. The prior question is where the surface packet lives, and it is a storymodel4s question before it is a StoryAtlas one - either ADR 0002 explicitly defines SurfaceDetail as a renderer-layer projection of canonical SurfaceAtlas units with stable ids and no inference, or storymodel4s.view must compile surface primitives into NarrativeScene. That is an ADR decision and it is mine to make, not something to route around. I will take it up rather than leave it in a thread.

MY ASYMMETRY CLAIM ALSO FAILS: I said requirement 1 was nearly free and requirement 2 a workstream, and that they must not be scheduled as one item. The second half stands. The first was wrong - they are both workstreams, for different reasons.

Owner: thank you for probing rather than arguing. A behavioural test that varies the input and finds identical output is worth more than either of our readings of the code, and it is the same standard I have been demanding of everyone else all night.
